name: Climate Almanac
description: An open, versioned index of public climate data.

entries.title: Berkeley Earth Surface Temperature
entries.description: Independent global land and ocean surface temperature analysis with gridded fields and uncertainty estimates. Often used as a cross-check against government temperature indices.
entries.license: CC-BY-NC-4.0 (Berkeley Earth data page; commercial licensing by request)
entries.attribution: Berkeley Earth Surface Temperature Data
entries.notes: Licence checked 2026-10-31: Berkeley Earth's data page (https://berkeleyearth.org/data/, renders in a browser; curl gets 403) says "In general, Berkeley Earth's data is licensed under Creative Commons BY-NC 4.0 International for non-commercial use only", with commercial licensing by request to admin@berkeleyearth.org. The earlier string said CC-BY-NC-SA; the page has no ShareAlike term. "In general" leaves room for an individual product to differ.

entries.title: Bureau of Meteorology Climate Data Online
entries.description: Australia's national weather service's station climate data: daily and monthly rainfall, temperature and solar exposure observations and statistics for current and historical weather stations across Australia, searchable by map or text and downloadable per station.

coverage.spatial: Australia (station level, current and historical stations)
coverage.temporal: varies by station (start years not checked)

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (Climate Data Online page and Bureau of Meteorology copyright notice)
entries.attribution: Bureau of Meteorology, © Commonwealth of Australia. Licensed from the Commonwealth of Australia under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International licence.
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 (page title "Climate Data Online - Map search"). The page says "You can get daily and monthly statistics, historical weather observations, rainfall, temperature and solar tables, graphs and data", offers a text search and a map search by station, and links "Latest rainfall totals, daily and monthly data" and station listings. On 2026-11-01 it carried outage banners: "Some radar data, warnings, and observations are not available due to a technical issue" and "Data outage: Some data might not be available due to a Bureau-wide network outage. Data is in the process of being recovered." The csv format is assumed from CDO's per-station downloads and wasn't tested; station start years weren't checked. Larger or custom extracts go through BoM's data services requests page, which redirects to reg.bom.gov.au.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: the CDO page itself says "Unless otherwise noted, all material returned by Climate Data Online are licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International Licence." The copyright notice (https://www.bom.gov.au/copyright, redirected from /other/copyright.shtml) gives the preferred attribution quoted above. It also says "we do not allow you to use automated or manual techniques to hack, scrape or otherwise extract material from our site", so bulk use should go through BoM's data services rather than scraping.

entries.title: Climate TRACE Emissions Inventory
entries.description: An independent, facility-level inventory of greenhouse-gas and air-pollutant emissions built from satellite observations, remote sensing and models by a not-for-profit coalition: hundreds of millions of emitting assets across 10 sectors and 67 sub-sectors, aggregated by city, state and country, with monthly data since 2021.

access.auth_note: The public API is a beta: "we cannot guarantee availability ... please keep volume low".

coverage.spatial: global (source, city, subnational and country level)
coverage.temporal: 2015-2025 annual, monthly from 2021; release 5.12.0 runs through August 2026

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (Climate TRACE terms of use; some external datasets such as EDGAR and FAOSTAT keep their own terms)
entries.attribution: Climate TRACE, using the suggested citation in its data guide, indicating any changes made
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200. The home page says "Track Global Emissions from 745 million sources of greenhouse gases and air pollutants worldwide", "Built by a global not-for-profit coalition of over 100 universities, scientists, and AI experts", "Group emissions by 10 industrial sectors broken into 67 sub-sectors", and "Follow 10+ years of data (2015-2025) with monthly data available from 2021". The data page (https://climatetrace.org/data) shows "Latest Data Release Oct 29, 2026 ... October release 5.12.0 includes monthly emissions data through August 2026", a country/sector download tool, geopackage boundary files, a "Public API Beta", and says "Previous versions of Climate TRACE data can be found on Zenodo." Climate TRACE estimates are modelled, not reported inventories; they complement the official UNFCCC data. The csv format is assumed from the download packages and wasn't opened; the API wasn't called.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: https://climatetrace.org/terms says "The emissions data and associated metadata has been made available via Climate TRACE under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License (CC BY 4.0), with the exception of external datasets listed below", and that users may reuse it "for any purpose, including commercial use, as long as you attribute it to Climate TRACE and indicate if you have made any changes". The listed exceptions include country-level estimates for several sectors taken from EDGAR and FAOSTAT, facility data from E-PRTR, US EPA FLIGHT and LMOP, Israel's PRTR and Canada's GHGRP, and ownership data from sources such as OpenCorporates and Wikipedia.

entries.title: ERA5 Reanalysis (single levels)
entries.description: Fifth-generation ECMWF global atmospheric reanalysis at ~31 km resolution, hourly from 1940 to near-present. The standard open reanalysis for weather and climate research when a consistent gridded product is needed.

access.auth_note: Free Copernicus Climate Data Store account required
access.rate_limit: CDS queue-based retrieval; see CDS fair-use policy

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (Copernicus Climate Data Store; replaced the Licence to use Copernicus Products on 2025-07-02)
entries.attribution: Copernicus Climate Change Service (C3S) (2025): ERA5 reanalysis. ECMWF.
entries.notes:
Native hourly fields; catalogue also offers monthly aggregates.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the CDS catalogue API for reanalysis-era5-single-levels returns "license": "CC-BY-4.0", and the dataset page's Licence heading reads "CC-BY licence". ECMWF announced (https://forum.ecmwf.int/t/cc-by-licence-to-replace-licence-to-use-copernicus-products-on-02-july-2025/13464) that CC-BY replaced the Licence to use Copernicus Products across the CDS, ADS and EWDS on 2 July 2025.

entries.title: CPC Long-Lead Climate Outlooks
entries.description: NOAA Climate Prediction Center seasonal and long-lead outlooks for temperature, precipitation, and drought across the United States. Operational guidance products for planners and researchers tracking climate variability.
entries.license: public-domain (US Gov work)
entries.attribution: NOAA/NWS Climate Prediction Center
entries.notes: Parent /products/predictions/ path returned HTTP 403 to automated probes but this long-range subdirectory responded 200 on 2026-06-29.

entries.title: DWD Open Data Server (Deutscher Wetterdienst)
entries.description: Germany's national meteorological service's open data server: the Climate Data Center's station observations for Germany (1-minute to annual and multi-annual values), gridded climate data, regional averages and global observations, alongside weather forecasts, numerical weather prediction output, radar, warnings and satellite products, all as files without registration.

coverage.spatial: Germany (station and grid level), with European grids and global observations
coverage.temporal: varies by product (start years not checked)

entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (CDC Terms_of_use on opendata.dwd.de and DWD legal notice)
entries.attribution: Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD), with a source note (Quellenvermerk) per https://www.dwd.de/copyright
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200. The root is a plain directory listing ("Index of /") with climate_environment/ and weather/, both updated 2026-11-01. README.txt says "Within its legal mandate, DWD offers weather and climate data free of charge on its Open Data server at https://opendata.dwd.de. Access is granted without registration." The Climate Data Center folder (/climate_environment/CDC/) holds observations_germany, observations_global, grids_germany, grids_europe, regional_averages_DE, derived_germany and event_catalogues; observations_germany/climate/ runs from 1_minute to annual and multi_annual; daily/kl/recent/ held station zip files dated 31-Oct-2026. The weather/ folder holds alerts, nwp, radar, satellite, local and text forecasts. grib2 is the usual NWP format and wasn't opened; the txt-in-zip format of station files is assumed from the names. Start years per product weren't checked.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: https://opendata.dwd.de/climate_environment/CDC/Terms_of_use.pdf reads "Terms of use for data on the CDC-OpenData area: The Creative Commons BY 4.0 - Licence 'CC BY 4.0' apply. For detailed information see https://www.dwd.de/copyright. Status: Mai 2024." That link redirects to DWD's legal notice (https://www.dwd.de/DE/service/rechtliche_hinweise/rechtliche_hinweise_node.html), which says (in German) that all freely accessible geodata and DWD's high-value datasets may be reused "unter den Bedingungen der Lizenz Creative Commons BY 4.0 (CC BY 4.0) unter Beigabe eines Quellenvermerks" (under CC BY 4.0, with a source note), and that content with third-party rights is marked as such. The README also notes DWD stores visitors' IP addresses for up to 7 days.

entries.title: Japan Meteorological Agency Past Weather Data (過去の気象データ検索)
entries.description: The Japan Meteorological Agency's archive of station observations across Japan: hourly, daily, ten-day, monthly and annual values of temperature, precipitation, wind, sunshine, snow and more for its observing stations, with climatological normals, searchable by station and date and downloadable as CSV.

coverage.temporal: varies by station; search offers years through 2026 (start years not checked)

entries.license: PDL-1.0 (Public Data License Version 1.0, JMA website terms of use; stated as compatible with CC-BY-4.0)
entries.attribution: Source: Japan Meteorological Agency website (URL of relevant page); state if the content was edited
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200. The issue's URL https://www.data.jma.go.jp/ is only a meta refresh to JMA's home page (https://www.jma.go.jp/jma/index.html), so this entry points at the data itself. The search page (title "気象庁｜過去の気象データ検索", Past weather data search) reads "地点と年月日時を選択して、表示するデータの種類を選択してください" (choose a station and date, then the data type) with year options from 2026 back; the old /obd/stats/etrn/ path redirects here. CSV downloads are on the companion page https://www.data.jma.go.jp/risk/obsdl/index.php ("過去の気象データ・ダウンロード", with a "CSVファイルの形式" help link; read in headless Chromium). Both pages are in Japanese; the English "Climate of Japan" page (https://www.data.jma.go.jp/stats/data/en/index.html) offers "Tables of Climatological Normals (1991–2020)" and "Tables of Monthly Climate Statistics". Station start years, the full list of elements and any API weren't checked.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: JMA's terms of use (https://www.jma.go.jp/jma/en/copyright.html) say "Information made available on the Japan Meteorological Agency website ('Content') may be used in accordance with the terms and conditions of use stipulated in Public Data License (Version 1.0), unless otherwise indicated by a specific rights notice", require citing the source (e.g. "Source: Japan Meteorological Agency website (URL of relevant page)") and marking edits, and say "The Terms of Use are compatible with the Creative Commons Attribution License 4.0 ... Content based on the Terms of Use may be used under the CC License in lieu of the Terms of Use." Use may also be limited by the Meteorological Service Act (forecasting licences, warnings), which doesn't affect past observations.

entries.title: EDGAR - Emissions Database for Global Atmospheric Research
entries.description: The European Commission Joint Research Centre's independent global inventory of anthropogenic greenhouse-gas and air-pollutant emissions, built with a consistent IPCC methodology from international statistics: national totals by sector for every country and 0.1-degree gridmaps, annual from 1970 with monthly data for recent years.
entries.license: CC-BY-4.0 (EDGAR_2026_GHG conditions of use), except the IEA-EDGAR fossil CO2 component, which is CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0
entries.attribution: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (JRC), EDGAR Community GHG database (IEA-EDGAR CO2, EDGAR CH4, EDGAR N2O, EDGAR F-gases), version EDGAR_2026_GHG (2026); full citation on each dataset page
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200. The home page says "EDGAR is a multipurpose, independent, global database of anthropogenic emissions of greenhouse gases and air pollution on Earth" that "provides independent emission estimates compared to what reported by European Member States or by Parties under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)", as "national totals and gridmaps at 0.1 x 0.1 degree resolution at global level, with yearly, monthly and up to hourly data". The data page (https://edgar.jrc.ec.europa.eu/emissions_data_and_maps) lists "EDGAR_2026_GHG 1970-2025 (CO2, CH4, N2O, F-gases)" plus air-pollutant, food, toxic-pollutant, HTAP and temporal-profile datasets. The 2026 report says "global GHG emissions in 2025 reached 54.1 Gt CO2eq". The EDGAR_2026_GHG page (https://edgar.jrc.ec.europa.eu/dataset_ghg2026) links 91 zip files on jeodpp.jrc.ec.europa.eu (one, EDGAR_CH4_1970_2025.zip, answered 200, 5.7 MB); gridmap archives are named *_nc.zip. The xlsx format inside the country-total zips is assumed and wasn't opened. This entry covers the whole database; the air-pollutant datasets' licences weren't checked.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: the site's terms page (https://edgar.jrc.ec.europa.eu/terms) says "Users are obliged to consult and refer to the full citation and conditions of use available on each specific dataset webpage." The EDGAR_2026_GHG conditions of use say "Unless otherwise noted, all material owned by the European Union is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) licence", and that IEA-EDGAR CO2 data "are based on data from IEA (2025) Greenhouse Gas Emissions from Energy ... as modified by the Joint Research Centre, licensed under CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. Users of the IEA-EDGAR CO2 data should contact the IEA at compliance@iea.org if they wish to use such data outside the terms of the CC-BY-NC-ND 4.0 licence." So fossil CO2 is non-commercial, no-derivatives; CH4, N2O and F-gases are CC BY 4.0.

entries.title: HadCRUT5 Global Temperature Dataset
entries.description: Met Office Hadley Centre / UEA CRU gridded near-surface temperature anomalies on a 5° grid. One of the long-running global temperature records used in IPCC assessments alongside NASA and NOAA products.
entries.publisher: UK Met Office Hadley Centre / Climatic Research Unit
entries.license: Open Government Licence v3.0 (UK Met Office data)
entries.attribution: HadCRUT5 — Met Office Hadley Centre / University of East Anglia

entries.title: GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP v4)
entries.description: NASA's global land–ocean surface temperature anomaly product, widely cited in annual global temperature reporting. Gridded anomalies and station-based analysis with open data files and documented methods.
entries.publisher: NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies (GISS)
entries.license: public-domain (US Gov work)
entries.attribution: NASA GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP Team, 2025)

entries.title: GRACE/GRACE-FO Land Mass Concentration (Mascon) Time Series
entries.description: NASA/JPL gridded time series of terrestrial water storage changes from the GRACE and GRACE-FO gravity missions. Used for drought, groundwater, and ice mass balance studies at regional to global scales.
entries.publisher: NASA JPL Physical Oceanography Distributed Active Archive Center (PO.DAAC)

access.auth_note: Free NASA Earthdata Login required for PO.DAAC downloads

entries.license: public-domain (US Gov work)
entries.attribution: NASA JPL GRACE/GRACE-FO Mascon solutions via PO.DAAC
entries.notes: Legacy grace.jpl.nasa.gov product pages returned 404 on 2026-06-29; PO.DAAC is the current canonical distribution path for this mascon release.

entries.title: NOAA Climate Data Online (CDO)
entries.description: Searchable archive and API for NOAA/NCEI station, radar, and derived climate datasets. The general-purpose access path for many NCEI holdings beyond single-product landing pages.

access.auth_note: Free NCEI token required for API access
access.rate_limit: 5 requests per second; 10,000 requests per day (documented CDO limits)

entries.license: public-domain (US Gov work)
entries.attribution: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, Climate Data Online

entries.title: Global Ocean Heat Content (NCEI)
entries.description: Observed ocean heat content anomalies for the upper ocean layers, a key indicator of Earth's energy imbalance and climate change. Maintained by NCEI as part of global ocean monitoring products.
entries.license: public-domain (US Gov work)
entries.attribution: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, Global Ocean Heat Content

entries.title: NOAA Storm Events Database
entries.description: Official record of severe storms and significant weather phenomena across the United States, with fatalities, injuries, and property damage. Widely used for hazard climatology and disaster research.
entries.license: public-domain (US Gov work)
entries.attribution: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, Storm Events Database

entries.title: U.S. Climate Normals
entries.description: NOAA NCEI's official climate-normal products describe typical conditions at nearly 15,000 U.S. weather stations. The current release provides annual, seasonal, monthly, daily, and hourly temperature, precipitation, and other climatological statistics for the 1991–2020 period.
entries.license: public-domain (US Gov work)
entries.attribution: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, U.S. Climate Normals
entries.notes: The 1991-2020 release is the current conventional 30-year normals period; NCEI also provides supplemental 15-year normals.

entries.title: Billion-Dollar Weather and Climate Disasters
entries.description: Database of US weather/climate disasters each exceeding $1B in damages (CPI-adjusted), 1980-present, with event-level cost, deaths, and type. The canonical record for US climate-disaster cost trends.

recovery.notes: Wayback capture made while the resource was live.
Capture from before NOAA announced in 2025 that it would stop updating the database: the state of the record while it was still maintained.

entries.license: public-domain (US Gov work)
entries.attribution: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information (NCEI), U.S. Billion-Dollar Weather and Climate Disasters
entries.notes: THE THESIS ENTRY. NOAA announced in 2025 it would stop updating this database. Historical data through 2024 remains reachable but is no longer maintained — hence status=frozen. This is exactly the kind of small, high-value, at-risk artifact that should be prioritized for an actual mirror (it is a single modest CSV). Verify current reachability before relying on it; if the page 404s, flip status to dark and populate archive.wayback_url + archive.mirror.

entries.title: Climate at a Glance — Global & National Time Series
entries.description: Monthly temperature and precipitation anomalies for the globe, nations, US regions, states, and counties. NCEI's flagship public-facing trend product; the source behind most "warmest year on record" reporting.

access.rate_limit: NCEI access API, no published hard limit; be polite

recovery.notes: Wayback capture made while the resource was live.

entries.license: public-domain (US Gov work)
entries.attribution: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, Climate at a Glance
entries.notes: Core dataset — high priority to keep mapped. Time series are small (CSV per region) and would be cheap to mirror if it ever darkens.

entries.title: Global Historical Climatology Network — Daily (GHCN-Daily)
entries.description: Daily station observations of temperature, precipitation, and snow for tens of thousands of land stations worldwide. The backbone of many global and regional climate analyses and a primary input to gridded products.
entries.license: public-domain (US Gov work)
entries.attribution: NOAA National Centers for Environmental Information, GHCN-Daily
entries.notes: Bulk files are served under /data/global-historical-climatology-network-daily/. Station metadata and documentation ship with the download bundles.

entries.title: Global Monitoring Laboratory — CO₂ Trends
entries.description: Atmospheric carbon dioxide measurements from the Mauna Loa and global in situ network, including the iconic Keeling Curve. The reference time series for anthropogenic CO₂ increase in public communication and research.

coverage.spatial: global (in situ sites; Mauna Loa flagship)

entries.license: public-domain (US Gov work)
entries.attribution: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory, Carbon Cycle Greenhouse Gases

entries.title: North American Snow Cover Extent (Rutgers Global Snow Lab)
entries.description: Weekly snow cover extent for North America (with and without Greenland) from the Rutgers Global Snow Lab's 190 km record, kept since late 1966 and archived by NOAA as the Northern Hemisphere Snow Cover Extent Climate Data Record. Complements sea-ice products for cryosphere and hydrology monitoring.
entries.publisher: Rutgers Global Snow Lab (NOAA Climate Data Record Program)

coverage.spatial: North America (also Eurasia and the Northern Hemisphere)

entries.license: no restrictions on use (NOAA CDR Program open data policy, Snow Cover Extent CDR use agreement); citation requested
entries.attribution: Robinson, D. A., Estilow, T. W., and NOAA CDR Program, NOAA Climate Data Record of Northern Hemisphere Snow Cover Extent, doi:10.7289/V5N014G9
entries.notes:
Identity corrected 2026-10-31. This entry previously named G02135 and pointed at https://nsidc.org/data/g02135, which is NSIDC's Sea Ice Index (cataloged separately as nsidc-sea-ice-index), and its DOI 10.7265/N5H1308K returned 404 from DataCite. The product the description named, the Rutgers Global Snow Lab's weekly North American snow cover, is the record repointed to here. The id is kept so existing links to it don't break.
Human-verified 2026-10-31: https://climate.rutgers.edu/snowcover/ returned HTTP 200 and describes "The original weekly snow extent record, from 1966 to present", with maps, tables and rankings from the 190 km data. Its monthly area table (https://climate.rutgers.edu/snowcover/190km/table_area.php?ui_set=1) has columns for the Northern Hemisphere, Eurasia, North America, and North America without Greenland, back to 1966. NOAA archives the record as the Snow Cover Extent (Northern Hemisphere) CDR (https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/products/climate-data-records/snow-cover-extent), which combines weekly maps (1966 to May 1999) with daily output from June 1999. Its landing page gives the DOI and netCDF downloads.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the CDR's use agreement (https://ncei.noaa.gov/pub/data/sds/cdr/CDRs/Snow_Cover_Extent_Northern_Hemisphere/UseAgreement_01B-12.pdf) says "the CDR data sets are nonproprietary, publicly available, and no restrictions are placed upon their use", and asks users to cite the data and acknowledge its developers. The record was developed at Rutgers University, so it is not labelled a US Government work.

entries.title: Sea Ice Index
entries.description: Daily and monthly Arctic and Antarctic sea ice extent and concentration, with anomaly fields and trend imagery. The standard reference for sea-ice decline; widely cited and surfaced by climate.gov.

recovery.notes: Wayback capture made while the resource was live.

entries.license: unverified — no licence stated; NSIDC requires citation as a condition of use (G02135 landing page)
entries.attribution: Fetterer, F. et al. Sea Ice Index, NSIDC, Boulder, Colorado USA
entries.notes:
Hosted at NSIDC (a university-based DAAC), so somewhat insulated from federal site shutdowns — but funded partly through NOAA/NASA, so not immune. Worth watching.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the earlier "public-domain (US Gov work)" label is not supported. The landing page (https://nsidc.org/data/g02135) says "As a condition of using these data, you must cite the use of this data set" and states no licence; NSIDC's data use page (https://nsidc.org/about/data-use-and-copyright) asks for a data citation, and its copyright statements cover the website, not the data. NSIDC is part of CIRES at the University of Colorado Boulder and the dataset's authors include university staff, so it is not shown to be a US Government work. The DOI is updated to Version 4 (10.7265/a98x-0f50, which resolves to /versions/4, where the link checker already lands); the old DOI 10.7265/N5K072F8 resolves to Version 3.

entries.title: UNFCCC Greenhouse Gas Inventory Data Interface
entries.description: The UNFCCC secretariat's interface to the national greenhouse-gas inventories that Parties report under the Convention: time series, detailed data by Party, comparisons by gas and category, GHG profiles and flexible queries for Annex I and non-Annex I Parties, plus Kyoto Protocol compilation and accounting data.
entries.publisher: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) secretariat

coverage.spatial: Parties to the Convention (Annex I in detail; non-Annex I from national communications and biennial update reports)
coverage.temporal: base year and 1990 onward; the Annex I time series showed a last inventory year of 2021

entries.license: public domain with conditions: official data may be freely copied provided no change to the content is introduced and the source is acknowledged (UNFCCC terms of use)
entries.attribution: UNFCCC secretariat, Greenhouse Gas Inventory Data (di.unfccc.int)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200, but plain curl gets only an Incapsula bot-protection script; headless Chromium with a desktop user agent and a 15-second wait rendered it. The root redirects to https://di.unfccc.int/time_series ("Greenhouse Gas Inventory Data - Time Series - Annex I"), with modules "Detailed data by Party, Comparison by Category, Comparison by Gas, GHG profiles, Global map - Annex I, Flexible queries, User-defined indicators, Compilation and Accounting Data", an "Export to Excel" button, and a table of GHG totals without LULUCF in kt CO2 equivalent whose columns run from the base year to "Last Inventory Year (2021)". UNFCCC's page on the data (https://unfccc.int/topics/mitigation/resources/registry-and-data/ghg-data-from-unfccc) says "The secretariat has completed the upgrade of all nine modules of the GHG data interface on 8 November 2019." The interface looks behind the latest submissions: its newest inventory year is 2021, though Annex I Parties submit annually and reporting under the Paris Agreement's Enhanced Transparency Framework began in 2024. Whether newer data lives in another UNFCCC tool wasn't checked. Climate-almanac should set reachability.headless for this entry.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: UNFCCC terms of use (https://unfccc.int/this-site/terms-of-use, read in headless Chromium) say "All official texts, data and documents, including low resolution webcast transmissions, are in the public domain and may be freely downloaded, copied and printed provided no change to the content is introduced, and the source is duly acknowledged." The same page also grants general site content only "for the User's personal, non-commercial use, without any right to resell or redistribute them or to compile or create derivative works therefrom", "subject to more specific restrictions that may apply to specific Content". Inventory data is official data, so the public-domain sentence is taken to apply, but the "no change to the content" condition is unusual and a steward may want UNFCCC to confirm it.

entries.title: U.S. Drought Monitor
entries.description: Weekly map and tabular summary of drought conditions across the United States, blending physical indicators and expert synthesis. The operational drought status record cited in media, agriculture, and policy.
entries.license: unverified — no data licence stated; © National Drought Mitigation Center (UNL), whose permission page asks for a set credit line when the map is reproduced
entries.attribution: U.S. Drought Monitor — USDA, NOAA, and University of Nebraska–Lincoln
entries.notes: Licence checked 2026-10-31: the earlier public-domain label is not supported. The USDM is produced by the National Drought Mitigation Center at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln with USDA, NOAA and NASA, so it is not a US Government work, and the site footer reads "©2026 - National Drought Mitigation Center". The permission page (https://droughtmonitor.unl.edu/About/Permission.aspx) asks that a reproduced map carry: "The U.S. Drought Monitor is jointly produced by the National Drought Mitigation Center at the University of Nebraska-Lincoln, the United States Department of Agriculture, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the National Aeronautics and Space Administration. Map courtesy of NDMC." The data citation page states no licence either.

entries.title: USGS National Water Information System (NWIS)
entries.description: Real-time and historical streamflow, groundwater, water quality, and related measurements from USGS monitoring networks. The primary federal portal for US hydrologic observations used in drought, flood, and climate-impact studies.

access.rate_limit: Documented NWIS web service limits; be polite

entries.license: public-domain (US Gov work)
entries.attribution: U.S. Geological Survey National Water Information System
